title: Passport stamps
rule: Sovereign states only; self-governing territories and disputed regions don't count.

traps.Taiwan: Self-governing, but it isn't counted as a UN member state.
traps.Kosovo: Declared independence in 2008, but it isn't a UN member state.
traps.Palestine: Has observer status at the UN, not full member status.
traps.Greenland: An autonomous territory of Denmark, not a sovereign country.
traps.Hong Kong: A special administrative region of China, not a separate country.

fact: Vatican City covers about 0.44 square kilometres, making it the world's smallest sovereign state.

title: Capital idea
rule: Where a country has more than one capital, any of them counts.

traps.Istanbul: Turkey's largest city, but not the capital.
traps.Sydney: Australia's biggest city, but not the national capital.
traps.New York: The largest US city, but not the capital.
traps.Rio de Janeiro: A former capital of Brazil, not the current one.
traps.Edinburgh: A UK nation's capital, but this card counts capitals of sovereign countries.
traps.Cardiff: A UK nation's capital, but this card counts capitals of sovereign countries.
traps.Belfast: A UK nation's capital, but this card counts capitals of sovereign countries.

fact: Nauru has no official capital, so Yaren is only the de facto seat of government.

title: Sightseeing
rule: Landmarks inside Greater London count, not ones elsewhere in England.

traps.Eiffel Tower: A famous landmark, but in Paris.
traps.Statue of Liberty: A famous landmark, but in New York.
traps.Edinburgh Castle: A famous castle, but in Scotland.
traps.Stonehenge: A prehistoric monument on Salisbury Plain, not in London.

fact: Kensal Green Cemetery, opened in 1833, was one of London's first large garden cemeteries.

title: Green space
rule: Royal parks, commons and heaths count when they're inside London.

traps.Central Park: A famous park, but in New York.
traps.Phoenix Park: A huge park, but in Dublin.
traps.Bois de Boulogne: A large park on the edge of Paris.
traps.Tiergarten: A large park in the middle of Berlin.
traps.Epping Forest: A forest on London's edge, but not a park in the usual sense.

fact: Coram's Fields in Bloomsbury only lets adults in when they are accompanied by a child.

title: Gallery crawl
rule: Museums and galleries count if they're inside Greater London.

traps.Louvre: A famous museum, but in Paris.
traps.Metropolitan Museum: A famous museum, but in New York.
traps.Prado: A famous museum, but in Madrid.
traps.Rijksmuseum: A famous museum, but in Amsterdam.
traps.Guggenheim: A famous museum, but not in London.

fact: The Wellcome Collection is free to enter and grew out of Henry Wellcome's collection of medical objects.

title: Island time
rule: Islands that are part of the UK; Crown Dependencies don't count.

traps.Isle of Man: A Crown Dependency with its own government, not part of the UK.
traps.Jersey: A Crown Dependency, so it doesn't count.
traps.Ireland: Shared between two countries, so it doesn't count as a UK island.
traps.Corsica: A French island in the Mediterranean.

fact: Lundy's name comes from the Old Norse for puffin island, and puffins still nest there.

title: Sun and sea
rule: Islands in the Mediterranean, including the Adriatic, Aegean and Ionian seas.

traps.Madeira: An Atlantic island belonging to Portugal.
traps.Canary Islands: Atlantic islands, not in the Mediterranean.
traps.Zanzibar: An island off East Africa, in the Indian Ocean.
traps.Bali: An Indonesian island in the Indian Ocean.

fact: Kastellorizo is often called the easternmost inhabited Greek island, lying just off the Turkish coast.

title: Departures
rule: Any UK airport or airfield counts; Crown Dependencies don't.

traps.Dublin: An Irish airport, not in the UK.
traps.Schiphol: The main Dutch airport, in Amsterdam.
traps.Ronaldsway: An airport on the Isle of Man, which is a Crown Dependency.

fact: Biggin Hill was one of the RAF's key fighter stations during the Battle of Britain in 1940.

title: Channel surfing
rule: Free-to-air and pay channels both count; streaming apps and regional services don't.

traps.HBO: A US premium channel, not a UK one.

fact: BBC Alba broadcasts mainly in Scottish Gaelic and launched in 2008.

title: High street
q: A UK bank or building society
rule: Brands count even if they're now owned by another group, and closed ones count too.

traps.Bank of America: A US bank, not a UK one.
traps.Citibank: A US bank, not a UK one.
traps.Deutsche Bank: A German bank with a UK arm, not a UK bank.

fact: Nationwide is the largest building society in the world.

title: Riverbank
rule: Rivers that flow through the UK, including Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.

traps.Shannon: Ireland's longest river, but in the Republic of Ireland.
traps.Rhine: A river through Germany and the Netherlands.

fact: The River Cam was historically called the Granta in its upper reaches.

title: Battlements
rule: Castles in England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland count, ruined or restored.

traps.Neuschwanstein Castle: A famous castle, but in Germany.
traps.Chambord: A French château, not a British castle.
traps.Blarney Castle: An Irish castle in the Republic of Ireland.
traps.Bran Castle: A Romanian castle linked to the Dracula legend.

fact: Caerphilly Castle is the largest castle in Wales and is famous for its leaning tower.
